scope: Final MSc submission figures; plot-only rendering from frozen results

figures.title: Hawkes excitation kernels for EUR/USD
figures.caption: Conditional least squares and converged EM estimates from the same 97,952 EUR/USD events. The upper panels show the full fitted branching matrices. Each cell gives the expected number of direct events of the row type generated by one event of the column type under the fitted model. CLS integrates over its fitted 0-500 second support; EM integrates its exponential kernels to infinity. The spectral radii are 0.9784 and 0.9373. The lower panels show the first ten seconds of bid-up to bid-down excitation and bid-up to ask-up excitation: respectively the strongest shared off-diagonal interaction and the largest remaining difference in integrated strength. The blue steps show the saved CLS bins and the dashed orange lines the saved EM kernels.

figures.title: Time-rescaling residuals of the EUR/USD EM fit
figures.caption: Pooled fitted-compensator increments against unit-exponential quantiles. The central 99.9% is shown on linear axes and the complete range on logarithmic axes.

figures.title: Empirical and simulated count dispersion
figures.caption: Empirical Fano factors compared with the median and minimum-maximum range across 30 stored fitted-model simulations. The empirical value lies below all simulations at 1, 10 and 60 seconds and inside their range at 300 seconds.

figures.title: Latent-book projection and recovery under weak pressure
figures.caption: Native-event counts before and after projection, recovery scores for both streams, and the projected-stream full-sequence higher-rate-state probabilities inside and outside the known pressure periods.

figures.title: Stronger pressure is easier to detect
figures.caption: Recovery before and after projection across 30 pressure settings. The left panel introduces market orders and in-spread limit orders; the right also introduces top-of-book limit orders and cancellations. The affected book side alternates between successive pressure periods. The horizontal values are the total rate multiplier m=1+delta_p. Marker shape gives the fraction of time under pressure; open and filled markers distinguish latent and projected streams. Each setting contains one simulation. The dashed line marks the F1=0.7 evaluation criterion.

figures.title: Recovering a known directional-pressure period
figures.caption: Full-sequence probability of the fitted higher-rate activity state on the deterministic median-F1 example (seed 19), with the known directional-pressure period shaded. The state is identified by fitted activity rate; the displayed probability uses the complete sequence.

figures.title: Recovery accuracy across 50 controlled simulations
figures.caption: Paired F1 scores for the rate-and-imbalance threshold method and HMM on the same 50 simulation seeds. The HMM scores higher on 39 seeds, lower on 10, and ties on 1; the means are 0.728 and 0.831.

figures.title: Post-fill movement and fill proportions
figures.caption: The cumulative curves pool 26,236 and 15,303 valid post-fill records at s=0 and s=1. At movement x, the curve gives the percentage of valid fills with absolute five-second movement no greater than x. The right panel shows fills as a percentage of bid- and ask-side quote opportunities over each complete 600-second simulation. Thirty matched simulations are shown. Absolute movement measures magnitude; signed markout retains economic direction.

figures.title: Execution-value frontier
figures.caption: Thirty matched simulations at seven posterior-sensitivity settings. The upper panel shows fill proportions relative to each seed's s=0 baseline, with medians; the lower shows changes from s=0 in mean absolute five-second movement in ticks, with equal-seed means. The horizontal references mark half of baseline fills and zero movement change.
